records.question: How was the weight of calcified material on recovered CAU plates determined?
records.ground_truth_answer: CAU plates were defrosted, disassembled, and dried at 60°C until plate weight stabilized, then decalcified in 5% HCl until all calcified material dissolved. Remaining fleshy material was scraped, vacuum-filtered, dried, and weighed. The weight of calcified material was calculated by subtracting the weight of the PVC plate and fleshy material from the total weight of the recovered unit and converted to an accretion rate based on time in water.
ground_truth_chunks: CAU plates were defrosted, disassembled, and dried at 60°C until plate weight had stabilized, and then decalcified in 5% HCl until all calcified material had fully dissolved.

Any remaining fleshy, non-calcified material was then scraped onto filter paper, vacuum-filtered, dried, and weighed. The weight of calcified material was calculated by subtracting the weight of the PVC plate and fleshy material from the total weight of the recovered unit and converted to an accretion rate based on time in water.

records.section_heading: War impacts on net carbonate accretion rates
records.question: What were the GLM results (estimate, SE, t, R2, p) for the relationship between War and carbonate accretion rates reported in this section?
records.ground_truth_answer: Estimate = 0.45, SE = 0.16, t = 2.89, R2 = 0.20, p = 0.007; the section states carbonate accretion rates increased exponentially with increasing War.
ground_truth_chunks: Carbonate accretion rates increased exponentially with increasing War (GLM with logtransformed response variable, estimate = 0.45, SE = 0.16, t = 2.89, R2 = 0.20, p = 0.007; [Figure 5](#page-8-0)), and the model fit improved with the equatorial and near-equatorial Pacific Remote Island Areas (Jarvis, Howland, Baker, Kingman, and Palmyra) removed as outliers (estimate = 0.57, SE = 0.15, t = 3.93, R2 = 0.24, p < 0.0001).

The fastest accretion rates (2010–2019 mean ± standard error = 121.2 ± 8.9 mg cm-2 yr-1) were observed at the highest War site (Rose, mean War = 4.05 ± 0.01), and were consistently high across the other four high-War islands of American Samoa (53.2–99.8 mg cm-2 yr-1).
